hook: Jonathan Ross started what became Google's Tensor Processing Unit as an internal side project, then left to found Groq in 2016, building a chip architecture designed purely for AI inference. Groq's language processing units made the company one of the most closely watched hardware challengers to Nvidia. In December 2025 Nvidia took a non-exclusive license to Groq's technology and hired Ross along with most of Groq's engineering team, a deal that returned billions of dollars to Groq's shareholders and moved its founder inside the company his chips were built to compete with. Ross now works at Nvidia as its chief software architect, and has spoken candidly about the leadership mistakes he made running Groq for nearly a decade.

standing.watch: What the records leave open is the shape of the Nvidia arrangement and what comes after it. The license is described as non-exclusive, so Groq's technology is not exclusively Nvidia's, and the records do not say what Groq becomes now that most of its engineering team and its founder have moved. Ross has said publicly that his early leadership mistakes cost Groq three to four years of progress, which is the only account here of how he ran the company for nearly a decade. The lawsuits tracked on this site are pending or monitored with no development recorded, and none of them names Ross or his companies. The latest news items naming him are not about Groq or Nvidia, so the record does not show what he is doing at Nvidia beyond the title.
standing.record: The record here is short and mostly about two companies. Groq was founded in 2016 in Mountain View, after Ross led the team at Google that designed and implemented the original Tensor Processing Unit, which began as an internal side project. Groq's chips are called LPUs, language processing units, built specifically for AI inference rather than training. Nvidia is listed as a public company founded in 1993 in Santa Clara, and Ross is listed as an executive of it. The lawsuits on this site do not name Ross or his companies: they are Brandon Grossinger v. Anthropic PBC, GROSSINGER v. ANTHROPIC, PBC., and Thomson Reuters Enterprise Centre GmbH v. Ross Intelligence Inc., which was decided in February 2025 on the use of Westlaw headnotes to train a competing legal AI. The news stories naming him are mostly unrelated industry items, and the pattern that runs through the record is a career built on inference hardware, from the TPU to Groq to Nvidia.
standing.standing: Jonathan Ross now works inside Nvidia as its chief software architect, the company whose chips his own were built to challenge. The records show he founded Groq in 2016 and built it into one of the most closely watched hardware challengers to Nvidia, with language processing units designed purely for AI inference. In December 2025 Nvidia took a non-exclusive license to Groq's technology and hired Ross along with Groq president Sunny Madra and most of Groq's engineering team. That deal returned billions of dollars to Groq's shareholders and moved its founder inside the company his chips were built to compete with. His influence now runs through Nvidia's software work rather than through an independent challenger.
